modules.title: Java Syntax Core & Type System
modules.description: How the JVM executes bytecode, primitive vs reference types, and strict typing rules.

content.overview: Java is a statically-typed language where every variable must be declared with a data type before use. The compiler converts source code (.java) into bytecode (.class) which the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) executes across any OS platform.
keyPoints: 8 Primitive Data Types: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char, and boolean.
Reference Types: Classes, Interfaces, and Arrays stored on the heap with memory managed by Garbage Collection.
Type Casting: Implicit Widening (int to double) vs Explicit Narrowing (`(int) myDouble`).
String Immutability: Strings are immutable objects stored in the String Constant Pool for memory optimization.

modules.title: Core Pillars of Java OOP

content.overview: Java is founded on the 4 pillars of Object-Oriented Programming. OOP organizes code into reusable, modular classes that bundle state (fields) and behavior (methods) while protecting internal implementation details.
keyPoints: Encapsulation: Restricting direct access to object state via private fields and public getter/setter methods.
Inheritance (`extends`): Reusing superclass properties while enabling hierarchical domain modeling.
Polymorphism: Method Overloading (compile-time) and Method Overriding (`@Override` dynamic runtime dispatch).
Abstraction (`interface` and `abstract class`): Defining contracts and abstract behaviors separated from concrete implementations.

content.overview: The Java Collections Framework provides standardized data structure interfaces and implementations to store, manipulate, and query groups of objects with type-safe Generics.

from fastapi import Depends, APIRouter

router = APIRouter(prefix="/modules")

async def get_db_session():
    session = "MockDBSession"
    try:
        yield session
    finally:
        pass # Cleanup

@router.get("/")
async def list_modules(db = Depends(get_db_session)):
    return [{"id": 1, "title": "FastAPI Async Endpoints"}]

modules.title: Basic Concepts: Client-Server Architecture & Full Stack Flow
modules.description: How the 4 tiers of MERN work together in a decoupled production environment.

content.overview: The MERN stack is a JavaScript-only full-stack framework consisting of MongoDB (Database), Express.js (Backend Framework), React (Frontend UI Library), and Node.js (JavaScript Runtime). The React client executes in the browser and communicates with the Express REST API via JSON HTTP requests, which in turn queries MongoDB using Mongoose models.
keyPoints: Client-Server Separation: Decoupled frontend (Vite/React) and backend (Express/Node.js) communicating via RESTful API endpoints.
Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS): Express middleware configuring origin headers to allow secure requests from the React client.
State Synchronization: Managing remote data fetching, loading spinners, caching, and optimistic UI updates on the React client.
JWT Authentication: Node.js signs cryptographic JSON Web Tokens; React stores tokens in secure memory or cookies and attaches them to `Authorization: Bearer <token>` headers.
Environment Configuration: Storing sensitive secrets (MongoDB connection string, JWT secrets, port) inside `.env` files.

modules.title: Basic Concepts: Promises, Async/Await & Event Loop
modules.description: How JavaScript manages single-threaded non-blocking I/O operations.

content.overview: JavaScript is single-threaded with an Event Loop. Asynchronous operations (network requests, timers, file I/O) are delegated to browser/runtime APIs and resolve via Microtask/Macrotask queues.
keyPoints: Promises have 3 states: Pending, Fulfilled (resolved), and Rejected.
async functions always return a Promise; await pauses execution until the Promise resolves.
try...catch blocks handle rejected Promises gracefully without crashing the application.
Promise.all() and Promise.allSettled() handle concurrent async tasks.
